Internet & networking · 4/8

no-cache is not no-store

no-cache

  • Stores the response
  • Revalidates before every reuse

no-store

  • Never stores the response
  • Every request goes to the origin

no-cache means check first, not do not store

Internet & networking · 5/8

No max-age: a heuristic guess

lifetime = 10% × (Date − Last-Modified)

  • 10% a typical guess, not a fixed rule
  • Last-Modified modified 10 days ago gives about 1 day

Internet & networking · 6/8

s-maxage is for shared caches

Browser cache (private)

  • Reads max-age=60
  • Stale after 60 s

CDN (shared)

  • Reads s-maxage=600
  • Stale after 600 s

One response, two lifetimes

Internet & networking · 7/8

Vary: one copy per header value

  1. 1br request: MISS, store the br copy
  2. 2gzip request: no match, MISS, store the gzip copy
  3. 3br request: HIT on the br copy

Internet & networking · 8/8

Hashed names: a new build is a new URL

  1. 1app.3f9a1c.js: max-age=31536000, immutable
  2. 2Every visit: HIT, no trip to the origin
  3. 3Deploy: the HTML names app.8b2e7d.js
  4. 4New URL, new key: MISS, fetch once

Now change the headers yourself.

Each scene loads a matching preset in the simulation beside the player.

With max-age set to sixty,

requests at thirty and fifty-nine seconds are a HIT.

At ninety seconds the copy is stale, so the cache must revalidate.

The stale copy carries ETag v1.

The cache sends If-None-Match v1.

The origin answers 304, and the copy is fresh again.

no-cache stores the response but revalidates before every reuse.

no-store never stores it, so every request goes to the origin.

With no max-age and no Expires, a cache may guess a lifetime.

A common guess is ten percent of the time since Last-Modified.

A CDN is a shared cache.

For shared caches, s-maxage overrides max-age,

so the CDN keeps the copy fresh for ten minutes.

Vary Accept-Encoding makes the cache keep one copy per encoding.

A gzip request cannot reuse the br copy.

app.3f9a1c.js never changes, so it gets max-age of one year and immutable.

A new build gets a new name, so a new cache key.
